fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. The man doesn't stay in the garden. The text says the LORD God “…banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.” Right before that, the LORD God speaks of the man reaching out to take from the tree of life and living forever (Genesis 3:22). I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story.

Yes, baker. The woman tells the serpent that God has said, “You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.” Notice she even adds “or touch it.” She's repeating the warning, and she's not shrinking it down to something small. Then the serpent answers with, “You will not surely die.” Those two lines are going head to head.

Busy? Friend, I've been in the back of a junk drawer, and even I had a better excuse than that! The man's answer is, “I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.” He says nothing about work. He says he was afraid, and he says he was naked. That's the reason he gives for hiding.

Yes, baker! The text says He “…stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.” Cherubim AND a sword that whirls with flame. That's a security team nobody could sneak past, and I should know, I can't even sneak past my own cookie jar. I think the way back looks closed here, and that part is heavy. But the story isn't over.
